citation_note: Primary studies support IL-3-associated JAK2/STAT5 activation and CIS/CISH induction through a STAT5-responsive promoter; CISH is retained as the normalized target label.
evidence_summary: Composite primary-supported claim: IL-3 engages the IL3RA:CSF2RB receptor complex, activates JAK2/STAT5 signaling and induces the cytokine-inducible CIS/CISH feedback gene. This supplies a named intracellular continuation and target output for the existing IL-3 receptor scaffold.
limitations: CIS/CISH nomenclature and species context differ across the primary studies, and the shared beta-chain makes pathway selectivity context-dependent; the direct JAK2-to-STAT5 ordering is retained as evidence rather than a new graph edge. No SCI transfer, causal graph traversal or database confidence score is asserted.

evidence_summary: Composite primary-supported claim: IL-23 engages the IL12RB1:IL23R receptor complex, activates JAK2/TYK2-associated STAT3 signaling and supports IL17A output in antigen-specific T-cell systems. limitations: The normalized ligand label retains the p40/p19 IL-23 branch but must not be interpreted as IL-12 signaling; IL-23 also activates STAT4 and other branches, and IL17A output depends on prior T-cell state and cytokine context.
